=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (three leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves grouped closely at the shoot apex, forming a whorl)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): obtuse (rounded tip, not sharply pointed)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced widely, 5-7 pairs (clearly visible in close-up images, running parallel to midrib and curving toward margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface has a glossy appearance, likely due to waxy cuticle)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or pubescence on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, leaf blade appears sessile or nearly so)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is firm and brownish, suggesting early woody development)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: brownish-green (stem is greenish-brown, darker than leaves)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf base or node)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible when stem or leaf is damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base or petiole; not applicable as leaf is simple and not characteristic of Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling from different angles. Leaves exhibit minor holes and some brown spots, likely damage or senescence, but not extensive. The whorled arrangement is clearly visible at the apex. No flowers or fruits are present. The seedling is growing in leaf litter, but habitat is not inferred. All observations made based on visible morphology without speculation on identity.
